result.title: Stochastic Pruning of the DPO Computation Graph: 1.4x Faster Training and Lower Peak Memory
result.summary: Direct preference optimization (DPO) incurs training costs in output scoring, sequence execution, and backpropagation, so reducing supervision alone does not necessarily save computation. We introduce a unified framework for stochastic pruning of the DPO computation graph that independently samples response positions for scoring, response prefixes for execution, and preference branches for backpropagation. By making these selections before the corresponding operations, the framework omits computation at each stage of a training step. Our analysis characterizes the objective changes induced by position and sequence pruning and uses inverse-probability weighting to obtain a conditionally unbiased single-branch gradient estimator for the sampled objective. Controlled measurements show that position and sequence pruning primarily reduce peak memory, with most output-memory savings attributable to an implementation that retains full response supervision. Branch pruning yields a $1.426\times$ step-time speedup over a concatenated DPO baseline and reduces training time by about 30\% relative to stock DPO across two model families, with slightly lower mean accuracy and benchmark-dependent changes in open-ended scores. These findings relate the resource benefits of stochastic graph pruning to the computation omitted and the resulting changes in the training objective.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出对 DPO 计算图做随机剪枝：在响应位置打分、响应前缀执行与偏好分支反向传播三处独立采样，并用逆概率加权得到条件无偏的单分支梯度估计，在两种模型族上取得约 1.43 倍步时加速和约 30% 训练时间下降，准确率略降。
AI.relevance_reason: 按位置/前缀采样监督并用逆概率加权重构梯度的思路，可能为 latent 推理轨迹训练中的选择性步骤监督、贡献分配与训练成本控制提供可核查线索；但对象为纯文本偏好优化，与视觉证据保留的关系尚待判断。
